Intro To Position

NPR's Society & Culture Desk offers news, discovery and analysis of arts and culture to curious audiences on digital, radio, podcasts, social platforms and video. We also cover the many elements of culture—from television, film, music, books, the arts and the internet — to the moments when people come together for shared experiences large and small. We uplift voices and perspectives that enrich and deepen our understanding of today’s cultural conversations. We provide original reporting, insight, context and signature curation initiatives that set NPR apart as a relevant journalism and cultural institution.

The Petra Mayer Memorial Fellowship was established in memory of beloved NPR Books Editor Petra Mayer, by her parents, to support fellowships with NPR’s Culture News Team.

The Petra Mayer Memorial Fellow will play a vital role in every aspect of our work, while also learning the core tenets of public service journalism, media ethics and multi-platform reporting and producing. Working alongside top professionals in the field, fellows are given real-world, hands-on responsibilities.

The fellow will focus their term on Books We Love and the Book of the Day podcast, signature NPR products founded by Mayer. They will also assist reporters with research on critical stories, both long-term projects and breaking news. They will also learn the basics of production by researching and pulling tape, securing rights and excellent audio quality, and by learning to mix pieces featuring varied soundscapes. We will also look to our fellows for assistance in digital production, basic headline writing, creative selection of art and social media promotion.

job.title: Salesforce Business Analyst
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is seeking a strategic and collaborative Salesforce Business Analyst to join a dedicated team focused on innovating and maintaining our enterprise Salesforce CRM. NPR’s Salesforce ecosystem is a critical driver of our organizational mission, powering operations that range from newsletter subscriptions and donor management to supporting our nationwide network of Member organizations and digital experiences for millions of public media listeners.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between business objectives and technical implementation. Working closely with diverse stakeholders, product managers, and development teams, you will strategically design, document, and refine our Salesforce data model and platform architecture. The ideal candidate is a natural problem-solver who can translate complex requirements into elegant, scalable Salesforce solutions, communicating seamlessly across varying levels of technical expertise.

Responsibilities

  • Requirements Elicitation & Scoping: Facilitate collaborative workshops with stakeholders across NPR to elicit, analyze, and document business processes and functional requirements.
  • User Story Creation: Author clear, actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, and comprehensive process maps to guide development efforts.
  • Roadmap Alignment: Partner closely with Product Managers to evaluate incoming business requests, assess strategic value, and prioritize the Salesforce backlog.
  • Solution Design Collaboration: Collaborate with Senior Salesforce Administrators and Developers to design scalable solutions that optimize platform capabilities while safeguarding data model integrity.
  • Impact & Dependency Analysis: Partner with technical teams to assess how new requirements affect existing platform architectures, upstream/downstream integrations, and dependent business systems.
  • UAT & Enablement Leadership: Design user acceptance testing (UAT) scripts, coordinate testing cycles, and author end-user training materials to ensure seamless feature adoption.
  • Project Delivery Coordination: Serve as a functional lead on project teams, tracking project health, proactively managing delivery timelines, and keeping key stakeholders aligned.
  • Governance & Best Practices: Promote platform standards and Salesforce-native best practices across cross-divisional teams to minimize technical debt.
  • Relationship Management: Cultivate trusted partnerships with internal departments and cross-functional technology peers, fostering an environment of collaboration and mutual support.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum of four (4) years of dedicated experience in business analysis, requirements translation, and functional design within the Salesforce ecosystem.
  • Platform Knowledge: Solid working knowledge of core Salesforce capabilities, configuration options, security models, and declarative automation tools.
  • Project Delivery: Demonstrated success leading or driving functional phases of cross-functional Salesforce projects from discovery through to deployment.
  • Stakeholder Facilitation: Proven ability to facilitate requirements-gathering sessions with non-technical business partners and translate operational needs into technical specifications.
  • Platform Certification: Salesforce Certified Business Analyst certification

Preferred Qualifications

  • Industry Experience: Experience working with the Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) or deep familiarity with non-profit donor engagement and CRM processes.
  • Ecosystem Tools: Familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, integrations, or related digital communication components

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Requirements Engineering: Advanced proficiency in mapping business processes, writing robust user stories, and establishing clear acceptance criteria.
  • Communicative Clarity: Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with a proven ability to distill technical architectural concepts into plain-language value propositions for business leads.
  • Prioritization & Adaptability: Proven ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously, maintaining high-quality delivery amidst shifting timelines.
  • Analytical Problem Solving: Strong critical thinking skills, with an aptitude for identifying process bottlenecks and designing proactive, platform-native solutions.
  • Inclusive Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills with a commitment to building collaborative, inclusive relationships across technical and non-technical teams.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field, OR equivalent hands-on professional work experience.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $85,500 - $105,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

job.title: Vice President, Individual and Institutional Giving
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is entering a period that requires sustained growth in philanthropic revenue and a fundraising organization built to deliver it consistently. The Vice President, Individual & Institutional Giving leads that organization: a team of approximately 20 across institutional giving, planned giving, individual giving, and donor recognition, accountable for ~$75M+ in annual revenue.

This is a systems leadership role. The VP does not carry a personal donor portfolio. Their leverage comes from the performance of five direct reports and the fundraisers beneath them — from pipeline discipline, coaching, and the standards they set for how NPR shows up with its donors. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer and partnering closely with the VP, Digital Revenue & Operations, the VP builds the infrastructure and the talent that make growth repeatable rather than episodic.

Responsibilities

Revenue Leadership

  • Own delivery of ~$75M+ in annual revenue across institutional, planned, and individual giving, with accountability for accurate forecasting and early warning when performance diverges from plan.
  • Set portfolio strategy and capacity targets across the team, allocating fundraiser time toward the relationships with the highest potential rather than the highest familiarity.
  • Partner with the CDO and Finance to build multi-year revenue projections grounded in pipeline evidence.

Pipeline & Moves Management

  • Own the moves management discipline across all frontline teams: stage definitions, advancement criteria, portfolio review cadence, and the accountability that makes them real.
  • Work with the Executive Director of Development Operations to build the reporting that gives every fundraiser and manager a clear view of their pipeline, and use it to drive weekly and monthly decisions rather than quarterly retrospectives.
  • Set the quality standard for the briefing materials, proposals, reports, and engagement strategies the team produces, so that every executive donor meeting has a defined purpose and a defined next step.
  • Diagnose where relationships stall and address the cause — whether that is skill, capacity, strategy, or a gap in what NPR can offer.

Team Leadership & Fundraiser Development

  • Lead and develop five direct reports across institutional giving, planned giving, individual giving, and recognition, holding each accountable for team performance while building their capability as managers.
  • Define what excellent fundraising looks like at NPR and build the coaching, training, and evaluation practices that produce it, with clear expectations by level and visible paths for advancement.
  • Develop fundraisers into compelling representatives of NPR — people who understand journalism deeply, can articulate what it costs and why it matters, and can hold a substantive conversation with a sophisticated donor.
  • Attend donor meetings regularly as coach and observer, present to develop the fundraiser rather than to own the relationship.
  • Partner with the CDO and the People team on hiring, performance management, and org design as the team scales.

Stewardship & Donor Recognition

  • Oversee the design and rollout of a tiered donor recognition system that works across giving channels and can be adopted organization-wide.
  • Build stewardship practices that treat retention and upgrade as designed outcomes rather than byproducts of goodwill.

Capacity & Efficiency

  • Identify where AI and automation can absorb the research, preparation, drafting, and analysis that consume frontline time, and redirect the capacity created toward the work that requires a human being: relationship depth, judgment in the room, and the ability to make NPR’s mission land.
  • Bring fluency with current AI tools and the judgment to distinguish genuine leverage from novelty, and build a team culture where adoption is expected and evaluated.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with the VP, Digital Revenue & Operations to create a coherent donor experience across digital and frontline giving, with clear handoffs as donors move between channels.
  • Work with Member Station colleagues and the Network Growth team to coordinate donor engagement across the public media system.
  • Align fundraising priorities with editorial and executive leadership so that what the team is selling reflects where NPR is going.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

In the first year, you will:

  • Install pipeline standards. Define stages, advancement criteria, and conversion benchmarks across institutional, planned, and individual giving, and establish the review cadence that holds the team to them.
  • Define fundraising excellence. Publish skill expectations by level across all frontline roles, with an assessment approach and a development plan for every fundraiser on the team.
  • Launch tiered recognition. Design and implement a donor recognition structure built for adoption across NPR.
  • Free up frontline capacity. Identify the highest-cost manual work across the team, deploy AI and automation against it, and demonstrate the hours returned to donor-facing activity.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 15+ years of professional experience, including 7+ years leading multi-team organizations and managing through managers.
  • 5+ years in development. Experience in enterprise sales, executive search, or another discipline built on long-cycle, trust-dependent relationships is a strong substitute for a longer fundraising tenure, and we encourage those candidates to apply.
  • Demonstrated accountability for a revenue program of comparable scale, with evidence of sustained year-over-year growth.
  • Proven track record of building pipeline systems and coaching practices that improved team performance, distinct from personal production.
  • Fluency with pipeline data and CRM reporting, and a habit of using it to make decisions about where people spend their time.
  • Working fluency with AI tools and a track record of finding practical efficiency gains with them.
  • Strong listening, writing, and speaking skills, with the ability to represent a complex organization to sophisticated audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • An understanding of complex fundraising organizations or federated nonprofit models.
  • An understanding of media/public broadcasting organizations and the relationship between NPR and its Member Stations.
  • Experience leading teams through a period of rapid growth or structural change.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in work experience required.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $216,000-$240,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

#LI-REMOTE

$216,000—$240,000 USD

job.title: Artist Marketing Director, Southeast Asia
job.description: About ONErpm Founded in 2010, ONErpm is a global music solutions company with 43 offices and studios in 35+ countries with over 530 staff members across the world, with significant presence in Brazil, the U.S., Europe, and other markets. ONErpm encompasses distribution, label solutions, content production, publishing, and an innovative marketing group that includes in-house advertising and influencer agencies, ONErpm has a proven track record of providing local and global support to artists and creators at any stage of their careers. About The Role The Artist Marketing Director, Southeast Asia (Global Level 4) is responsible for leading and managing the Regional Marketing Project Management team. This role defines and executes the country-specific artistic marketing strategy in close collaboration with the head of Asia and the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), ensuring alignment with global business objectives while addressing local market opportunities. The Artist Marketing Director develops, oversees, and evaluates integrated marketing and communication strategies, including campaign planning and execution, sales promotion initiatives, advertising agency management, promotional activities, and market research. The role is accountable for driving market share growth, maximizing artist visibility and audience engagement, and enhancing the effectiveness of artist marketing initiatives across digital and social media platforms. This position also provides strategic leadership on local market trends, consumer behavior, and competitive dynamics, translating insights into impactful marketing programs that support client and artist success. This role reports directly to the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of ONErpm and the head of Asia. Responsibilities: Direct the evolution and implementation of artist and release marketing frameworks, spearheading high-impact album and single launches and consumer-centric digital campaigns designed to accelerate audience expansion and fan engagement. Act as the primary strategic conduit between artists, management, and ONErpm, cultivating robust professional relationships to ensure cohesive alignment on marketing targets and project execution. Collaborate cross-functionally with label services and internal business units to engineer and deploy innovative marketing programs that bolster artist releases, catalog optimization, and specialized initiatives. Lead the conceptualization, planning, and management of creative marketing strategies, ensuring all campaigns are synchronized with artist vision, market trends, and organizational priorities. Govern the development of project roadmaps, financial budgets, and critical deliverables, orchestrating departmental efforts to guarantee the seamless and timely delivery of marketing milestones. Assess campaign efficacy, market shifts, consumer behavior, and competitive intelligence to uncover growth opportunities, refine strategy, and deliver actionable data-driven insights to leadership. Coordinate and manage alliances with external stakeholders, including PR firms, radio promotion specialists, booking agents, and industry partners, to optimize campaign reach and artist visibility. Provide mentorship and strategic direction to Marketing Project Managers and Coordinators, driving team productivity, career growth, and operational high performance. Manage the talent lifecycle—including recruitment, onboarding, and continuous training—to cultivate a sophisticated, high-performing, and collaborative marketing culture. Partner with senior executives to assess and authorize resource allocation for project management, supporting international marketing objectives and global expansion. Co-manage strategic digital alliances with top-tier platforms like Meta and TikTok, alongside emerging digital entities, in coordination with the Digital leadership team. Proactively identify, pitch, and secure premium digital marketing placements, original content opportunities, and promotional visibility for the ONErpm roster through key platform integrations. Establish and fortify strategic relationships with external industry bodies, including PROs, media organizations, and relevant music industry stakeholders. Ensure all marketing frameworks, partnerships, and tactical initiatives contribute meaningfully to artist development, fan acquisition, revenue streams, and market share growth. Qualifications Minimum 7 years of experience in artistic marketing or related roles within the music, entertainment, or media industry. Proven experience leading local marketing teams. Demonstrated success developing and executing large-scale marketing campaigns with measurable results. Deep understanding of music marketing, streaming ecosystems, audience growth strategies, and fan engagement. Experience managing cross-functional projects and collaborating with artists, managers, labels, agencies, and platform partners. Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting campaign performance data, KPIs, and ROI metrics. Experience overseeing media budgets, forecasting, and campaign optimization across multiple markets. Knowledge of influencer marketing, social media trends, and emerging digital platforms. Excellent communication, leadership, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Experience with CRM, audience data collection, and fan acquisition strategies including email, SMS, and retargeting. Ability to work effectively across diverse cultures, teams, and international markets. Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities with a results-driven mindset. Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Music Business, or a related field preferred. Ability to communicate fluently and effectively in English and one or more Southeast Asian languages (Mandarin, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Malaysia, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese)

Serving as both a subject matter expert and system steward, you will govern our content from creation and ingest through distribution, archival, and retention, while maintaining the integrity, accessibility, and discoverability of enterprise media assets. job.title: Sr Mgr, Talent Acquisition - US Corporate & Commercial
job.description: Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Garnet Hill® and Grandin Road. Your Opportunity, Your Team As Senior Manager, Talent Acquisition, you'll lead a significant portion of our TA function, guiding Managers and senior recruiting professionals as they deliver talent for the business. This isn't a role where you'll spend your days working a req list. You'll own the talent acquisition strategy for your area, from sourcing channel mix and pipeline development to employer brand activation and the operating model that ties it all together, and you'll build the systems and team capability that make great recruiting repeatable at scale. You'll report to the Senior Director, US Talent Acquisition, and you'll operate as a true business partner to functional leaders and HR leadership, advising on talent strategy, market dynamics, and hiring decisions at a level that shapes how the organization designs itself. You'll also drive our shift toward proactive talent acquisition, embedding a talent advisor mindset across your team so that recruiters show up as labor market analysts, career coaches, hiring strategists, and process change agents. If you're energized by building teams, frameworks, and capability rather than simply filling roles, and you want to help transform how a Fortune 500 company finds and hires talent, keep reading. Where You'll Work This role is hybrid and will require you to be onsite at our West Chester, PA headquarters (Studio Park) several days per month (onsite days are predetermined and standard across the company). Job seekers must reside in one of the following states to be considered: Pennsylvania, New Jersey, or Delaware. Relocation assistance is not available for this role. What You'll Do Lead and develop a team of TA professionals, setting the standards, coaching performance, and building the bench of future recruiting leaders. Own the proactive talent acquisition strategy for your area, including sourcing channels, pipeline development, talent community building, and employer brand activation. Advise senior business and HR leaders on talent strategy, labor market dynamics, and hiring decisions, earning a seat at the table on workforce planning and organizational design. Lead TA business planning for your area, including headcount demand forecasting, recruiter capacity modeling, and alignment to workforce plans. Build the KPI frameworks, capability programs, and accountability structures that make consultative, data-driven recruiting the norm across your team. Identify systemic gaps in how the function operates, design solutions, and drive implementation through your leadership team. Develop team capability in advanced sourcing, business partnering, data literacy, inclusive hiring practices, and candidate experience design. Partner with Total Rewards on compensation strategy and offer competitiveness, bringing forward hiring market patterns that should inform comp decisions. Set standards for full utilization of TA technology and data-driven recruiting practices, and hold leaders accountable for translating tools into measurable outcomes. Establish vendor governance for your area, holding search firms and platform vendors accountable to defined performance standards and ROI. Lead or co-lead cross-functional projects spanning process re-engineering, technology implementation, and organizational capability. Represent QVC Group externally in industry forums, employer brand events, and senior recruiting networks, strengthening our market presence and talent pipelines. Step into a small number of high-priority or sensitive searches when your direct involvement adds real value. What You'll Bring 10+ years of recruiting experience, including at least 5 years in progressively senior TA management roles. Experience managing managers and leading recruiting teams through other leaders, including coaching, performance management, and succession planning. A track record of driving TA transformation, whether shifting a team toward proactive sourcing, redesigning operating models, or building new capability at scale. Strong business partnering skills, with demonstrated credibility advising HR and senior business leaders on talent strategy. Fluency with recruiting data and analytics, and comfort using both to coach performance and influence decisions. Experience with TA technology, workforce planning, and organizational change. Commitment to inclusive sourcing and hiring practices. #LI-AI1 Our Total Rewards package includes benefits you’ll love such as competitive compensation, paid time off, an employee assistance program, parental leave, paid volunteer hours, and amazing company discounts! job.title: Account Executive, KBZK Bozeman
job.description: Are you a driven sales professional ready to help local businesses thrive? KBZK, serving Bozeman, Montana, is seeking an Account Executive, Local who will partner with businesses to deliver powerful advertising solutions that drive real results. This is your opportunity to combine strategic thinking with creative problem-solving while building lasting relationships in a community that values hard work and authenticity. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Sell advertising solutions to local and regional businesses and advertising agencies. Apply the Scripps Sales Process (SSP) to analyze current and prospective customer needs and apply customized advertising solutions that provide return on their investment. In addition to television commercial airtime sales, facilitate the customer's ability to take advantage of the full array of digital marketing options available. Independently prospect, secure appointments, perform needs analysis, develop customized solutions, present and close sales to develop and maintain new business from traditional and non-traditional advertisers. Use ratings data, qualitative information and market trends to negotiate program ratings and advertising rates with advertising agencies in order to maximize revenue as well as develop custom solutions for new advertisers. Serve as a trusted advisor with new and existing clients, provide best-in-class customer service, grow accounts, and gain additional business from referrals. Perform client services, including but not limited to media avail negotiations, presentation preparation delivery and execution, copy writing, credit applications and collection of revenue due. Effectively and proactively manage a sales funnel by way of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, monitoring and achieving key performance indicators and expected activity levels. Contribute to the creative development of campaigns though client communication and needs analysis, storyboard and concept creation, and assistance in production aspects. Build and maintain strong client relationships, which may include entertaining prospective and existing clients. Perform routine administrative functions of a media salesperson including makegood resolution, continuous update of CRM system with activity, account information and pending revenue, and communication with sales leadership regarding the status of accounts. Perform other duties as assigned. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience Generally 2+ years of proven sales success preferred Experience in strategic account management, broadcast ratings and digital execution preferred Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Highly self-motivated and goal focused Highly creative and innovative thinker Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills Effective teamwork and collaboration skills Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals Exceptional verbal and written communication skills Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels) Strong time management and organizational skills Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint) Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.) WHAT WE'LL OFFER: Uncapped sales commission Monthly allowance for mileage and cell phone Extensive Scripps Sales Process training A career path to grow your professional experiences Full medical, dental and vision benefits, as well as certain other health and wellness benefits Retirement savings plan with company match Other key company benefits include disability accident insurance, life insurance, ID protection, pet discount program, and employee assistance program. More details about timing and conditions of benefits eligibility and other plan terms and conditions will be provided upon hire. OUR TEAM: We have hikers, rock climbers, mountain bikers, kayakers, runners, skiers, fishing enthusiasts, boaters, and every other mixture of diverse backgrounds, passions, and life experiences. We are a community of welcoming, mission-focused, and lively people who continue to grow as we grow our company and rise to our full potential in every aspect of our business. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Bozeman, Montana, has a history still alive with the remnants of bygone days and sustains a local heritage that can still be found throughout the community, with nine historical districts and more than 40 individual properties listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The town of Bozeman provides a unique environment for a different kind of lifestyle and often tops lists of best places to live. It is blessed with relatively good weather, outstanding scenery, unparalleled recreational opportunities, world-class fishing, plenty of cultural activities, galleries, museums, and the like. Tech start-up companies are prevalent and growing in the area. The Bozeman area has served as a filming site for a number of films, including The Wildest Dream, A River Runs Through It, A Plumm Summer and Amazing Grace, and Chuck. Bozeman is a short (and beautiful) drive to Yellowstone National Park. Big Sky resort draws the world's wealthiest people as well as A-list celebrities. KMVT, the CBS affiliate serving Twin Falls, Idaho, is seeking an Account Executive who will partner with businesses to deliver powerful advertising solutions that drive real results. This is your opportunity to combine strategic thinking with creative problem-solving while building lasting relationships in a community that values hard work and authenticity. This is your opportunity to work with cutting-edge broadcast technology while supporting a team dedicated to serving the people of Green Bay and beyond. If you're passionate about solving complex technical challenges, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want to make a real impact, we want to hear from you! WHAT YOU'LL DO Provide world class customer service to all business partners internal and external to the Scripps organization with a positive "can do" attitude. Support, maintain, and install the full range of broadcast, Radio Frequency (RF), and production systems based on both Serial Digital Interface (SDI), and Internet Protocol (IP) based architecture. Setup and enhance software, hardware, server, automation and workflow systems, projects and equipment to enable our teams to be both productive and efficient. Ensure all meet current industry standards and comply with Company policies and expectations. Live truck technology may include microwave, satellite, cellular bonding, and video/audio equipment. Maintain logs and reports as per FCC Rules and Regulations. Provide, enhance, and utilize proactive monitoring system to anticipate technical issues and be able to act accordingly. You'll work alongside talented reporters and MMJs, helping them uncover deeper angles, strengthen their craft, and find new ways to connect with our community. Mentor, coach, and develop journalists at all experience levels through regular feedback and guidance. Oversee story writing and content development across broadcast, digital, and social platforms. Review content and provide timely, constructive feedback that drives continuous improvement. Develop and implement efficient workflows and editorial processes that support multiple news programs and platforms. Ensure all reporting and content meet high journalistic standards, ethical guidelines, and legal requirements. Foster a culture of trust, accountability, and collaboration among reporters, photographers, and newsroom staff. Scripps Company, is searching for an Executive Reporter to help lead our newsroom into the future. This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished journalist who excels at both storytelling and leadership. As Executive Reporter, you'll be a newsroom coach, content strategist, and trusted editorial voice, helping reporters and multimedia journalists elevate their work while contributing your own impactful journalism across platforms. You'll collaborate with newsroom leaders to shape content that matters to Western New York, develop journalists at every stage of their careers, and champion innovative storytelling that strengthens our connection with audiences. Review stories and provide actionable feedback to improve content quality, storytelling, and audience engagement. Help identify and develop high-impact enterprise, investigative, and community-focused stories. Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and continuous learning. Serve as a trusted editorial leader, ensuring content meets the highest standards of journalistic ethics, accuracy, and fairness. Work closely with producers, assignment editors, digital teams, and newsroom leaders to maximize the reach and impact of content. job.title: Lead AI Architect (Onsite - Hybrid)
job.description: The E.W. Scripps Company is seeking a Lead AI Architect to d esign and implement enterprise-scale AI solutions with a strong engineering foundation, bringing deep technical expertise in agentic systems, developer tooling, and AI platform integration. Contribute to the architectural strategy for AI-powered applications — including agent frameworks, tool ecosystems, and model provider integrations — and translate business requirements into production-grade systems built to last. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Define and own AI solution architectures spanning agentic workflows, MCP server infrastructure, and multi-model orchestration. Lead the design and deployment of complex RAG architectures and vector database strategies to support enterprise data retrieval. Architect and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and tool integrations, emphasizing advanced function calling and structured output schemas. Drive integration with major model providers (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and define standards for model selection, routing, and fallback. Establish engineering patterns for AI observability, prompt engineering, and rigorous AI evaluation frameworks to ensure reliability. Collaborate with engineering, product, and platform teams to deliver integrated AI solutions within existing software ecosystems. Ensure scalability, security, and maintainability through sound software architecture principles. Guide prototyping and proof-of-concept efforts; define technical evaluation criteria for emerging AI tools and frameworks. Present technical solutions and recommendations to senior stakeholders in a clear and compelling way. Mentor peers and establish best practices in AI engineering, agent design, and tooling. Uphold and define security, compliance, and responsible AI standards, specifically addressing OWASP LLM Top 10 risks, prompt injection, and PII leakage. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: BS/BA in Computer in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred Generally, 8+ years of experience in related field preferred Experience in AI/agent development strongly preferred Relevant certifications (AWS, Azure, cloud AI services) a plus Experience in the Media and Broadcast domain is a plus WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Advanced experience building and deploying production AI applications with a software engineering mindset. Hands-on expertise designing and deploying AI agents using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or similar. Deep understanding of RAG implementation patterns and vector database optimization. Proficiency setting up and managing MCP servers and defining tool schemas for LLM tool-use integrations. Strong experience integrating with cloud-hosted model providers — particularly AWS Bedrock and Azure AI Service. Proficiency in at least one backend programming language (Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Java, etc.) for building production AI systems. Familiarity with REST/GraphQL APIs, event-driven architectures, and containerized deployments (Docker, Kubernetes). Experience with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, and developer tooling in cloud environments. Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences. Understanding of AI safety, prompt security, and responsible AI practices. Awareness or experience with LLM fine-tuning is a plus. #LI-SM 2 #LI-Onsite If you are a current Scripps employee, please do not apply on this site. As Manager, Station Broadcasting, you'll be at the center of everything that keeps our station on-air and thriving. job.title: Multi-Media Managing Editor, WMAR
job.description: WMAR, The E.W. Scripps ABC Station in Baltimore, MD, is searching for a Multi-Media Managing Editor to help lead a new era of local news. We're looking for a newsroom leader who understands that today's audiences expect news wherever they are, whether that's on a streaming channel, a phone, social media, or television. You'll be at the center of our operation, helping drive a 24/7 news stream while ensuring the newsroom stays connected, informed, and focused on the stories that matter most. This role is part coach, part editor, and part conductor. You'll help reporters and MMJs tell stronger stories, make smart decisions in the moment, and find creative ways to connect our journalism with the communities we serve. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Lead the daily execution of WMAR's streaming and digital news coverage, ensuring audiences have access to timely, relevant content around the clock. Serve as the newsroom's central information hub, helping coordinate coverage plans, breaking news response, and content priorities. Coach and develop reporters and MMJs to elevate storytelling across digital, streaming, social, and broadcast platforms. Collaborate with newsroom leadership to execute audience-focused content strategies that drive engagement and community impact. Oversee the writing, editing, and publishing of stories across all platforms while maintaining quality and consistency. Provide timely and constructive feedback that helps journalists strengthen their reporting, writing, and presentation skills. Develop and refine workflows that support multiple news products, including streaming, digital, social, and broadcast content. Ensure all content meets the highest standards of journalistic ethics, accuracy, fairness, and legal compliance. Help identify opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting that resonate with local audiences. Support breaking news coverage and provide multi-platform content leadership when news demands immediate action. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Seven or more years of experience in journalism, digital content, newsroom leadership, streaming, or a related field preferred. Proven experience managing content in a fast-paced newsroom environment and making sound editorial decisions under deadline pressure. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Deep roots in digital journalism, streaming content, and audience engagement strategies. Strong understanding of broadcast-style storytelling and how to adapt stories across platforms. Demonstrated expertise in coaching journalists and helping teams produce stronger, more impactful work. Exceptional editorial judgment and knowledge of journalistic ethics, media law, and libel standards. Curiosity about the communities, issues, and people that shape the stories we cover every day. Strong organizational and communication skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. A collaborative leadership style that builds trust and encourages innovation throughout the newsroom. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment where priorities can shift quickly. Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays when news coverage requires it. OUR TEAM: WMAR is home to journalists who care deeply about serving Baltimore and Central Maryland. We're a collaborative team of reporters, photographers, producers, digital content creators, and newsroom leaders who believe local journalism should inform, connect, and strengthen the communities we serve. Our team is committed to impactful storytelling, breaking news excellence, accountability journalism, and meaningful community engagement. We embrace innovation, encourage new ideas, and support one another as we evolve for the future of local news. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Baltimore offers the energy of a major metropolitan area with the accessibility and character of a close-knit community. Located along the Chesapeake Bay and within easy reach of Washington, D.C., Baltimore is a city rich in history, culture, and opportunity. The region features vibrant neighborhoods, world-class healthcare and education institutions, thriving arts and entertainment districts, and some of the most diverse communities in the country. Whether you're exploring the Inner Harbor, attending Orioles or Ravens games, enjoying the city's renowned food scene, spending time on the waterfront, or discovering the unique stories that define Maryland's communities, Baltimore offers endless opportunities for both professional growth and personal enjoyment. It's a market where local journalism matters and where impactful storytelling can make a meaningful difference. At WMAR, you'll have the opportunity to lead coverage in a market known for passionate audiences, diverse communities, and stories that shape conversations across Maryland. #LI-SM2 #LI-Onsite COMPENSATION RANGE: Annual Salary: $100,000.00 - $120,000 Pursuant to state and local salary transparency laws, the salary range posted is specific to candidates who will perform this work in Maryland. job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KBZK
job.description: At KBZK, storytelling is more than a job. It's a chance to capture the people, places, and moments that make western Montana unlike anywhere else in the country. We're looking for a Multimedia Journalist who wants to immerse themselves in the community, chase meaningful stories, and bring them to life across multiple platforms. From breaking news and in-depth features to live reporting from the field, you'll be at the center of the stories that matter most to our viewers. If you're energized by journalism, inspired by mountain landscapes, and excited about making a real impact in a close-knit community, we'd love to meet you. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Develop story ideas by researching news leads, tips, and emerging community issues. Gather and verify information through interviews, observation, and in-depth research. Write compelling, accurate stories that meet broadcast and digital editorial standards. Shoot engaging video and capture still photography to support storytelling across platforms. Edit video content for on-air broadcasts, digital channels, and social media. Deliver live reports from the scene of breaking news, community events, and enterprise stories. Appear on-air for interviews, stand-ups, and story narration. Collaborate closely with photographers, producers, and digital teams to create impactful coverage. Assist in preparing daily newscasts and multimedia content plans. Consistently produce content that informs, connects, and serves the communities of western Montana. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in journalism, communications, or a related field preferred, or equivalent professional experience. Three or more years of experience in television news, multimedia journalism, or a related field preferred. Valid driver's license, good driving record, and the ability to provide proof of insurance meeting company requirements. Ability and willingness to travel throughout the viewing area to cover stories and community events. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Strong broadcast writing skills and knowledge of AP Style. Experience with videography and non-linear editing systems. Working knowledge of broadcast-quality camera equipment. Experience editing on Final Cut Pro or similar editing platforms. Proficiency with newsroom computer systems and digital publishing tools. Ability to post and optimize content for websites and digital platforms. A self-starter mindset with excellent time management and organizational skills. Sound news judgment and the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines. A collaborative approach and passion for community-focused storytelling. Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds of equipment when needed. OUR TEAM: At KPAX, you'll join a passionate group of journalists, photographers, producers, and storytellers who care deeply about serving their community. We believe great journalism starts with curiosity, authenticity, and teamwork. Our newsroom values diverse perspectives, fresh ideas, and a relentless commitment to telling stories that matter. You'll have the support to grow your craft while working alongside talented teammates who love what they do and where they live. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Nestled in the heart of the Rocky Mountains, Bozeman offers an unmatched blend of outdoor adventure, vibrant culture, and small-town charm. Surrounded by stunning mountain ranges and just a short drive from Yellowstone National Park, you'll find year-round opportunities for hiking, skiing, mountain biking, fishing, and exploring some of the country's most breathtaking landscapes. Bozeman's energetic downtown features locally owned restaurants, breweries, coffee shops, live music venues, and a thriving arts scene that gives the city a unique personality. Bozeman is also home to Montana State University, helping create a dynamic and innovative community that attracts entrepreneurs, outdoor enthusiasts, and creative professionals from around the country. With excellent schools, a strong sense of community, and easy access to world-class recreation, it's a place where professional growth and quality of life go hand in hand. job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KERO - Kern River Valley
job.description: At KERO 23 ABC, we believe every community deserves a journalist who knows its people, understands its challenges, and tells its stories with authenticity. As our Multimedia Journalist serving California's Kern River Valley, you'll be more than a reporter, you'll be the trusted voice covering a region whose stories often go untold by larger markets. This role is designed for someone who thrives working independently, building relationships, and becoming part of the fabric of a close-knit community. Nestled around Lake Isabella and surrounded by some of California's most stunning outdoor recreation, the Kern River Valley offers a unique lifestyle for journalists who value adventure, connection, and meaningful local storytelling. You'll have the opportunity to shine a spotlight on the issues, triumphs, and people that make this region special while ensuring local residents see their communities represented in the news every day. Deliver accurate, engaging live reports from the field. Cultivate sources and build strong relationships with community leaders and residents. Report on breaking news, public safety issues, weather impacts, and community events. Produce compelling digital content, including videos, articles, and social media updates. A passion for community-focused journalism and audience engagement. Confidence working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Proficiency with digital publishing tools, social media platforms, and mobile journalism techniques. Ability to adapt quickly to breaking news situations and changing priorities. Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as news coverage requires. Ability to safely lift and carry standard field reporting equipment and work outdoors in varying weather conditions. OUR TEAM: The KERO 23 ABC newsroom is made up of dedicated journalists who care deeply about the communities they serve. Our team brings diverse experiences, perspectives, and talents together to create meaningful journalism that informs, connects, and empowers viewers across Kern County and beyond. job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KPAX
job.description: At KPAX, we believe local journalism has the power to inform, connect, and strengthen communities. As a Multimedia Journalist, you'll play a key role in telling the stories that matter most to viewers across western Montana. From breaking news and community events to impactful enterprise reporting, you'll research, shoot, write, edit, and deliver compelling content across multiple platforms. You'll have the opportunity to build trusted relationships, uncover meaningful stories, and help audiences stay informed wherever they consume news. If you're a passionate storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Develop story ideas by evaluating news leads, tips, community trends, and daily assignments. Research, gather, and verify information through interviews, observation, and independent reporting. Write clear, accurate, and engaging stories aligned with broadcast and digital editorial standards. Capture high-quality video and still photography to support news coverage. Edit video content for television broadcasts, digital platforms, and social media channels. Deliver live reports from the field and provide real-time coverage of breaking news and community events. Appear on-air for story narration, interviews, and newscast presentations. Collaborate with photographers, producers, and newsroom colleagues to create impactful content. Support newscast preparation by contributing story elements, updates, and editorial input. Work closely with digital and online teams to enhance multimedia storytelling across platforms. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience. Three or more years of relevant journalism, reporting, or multimedia storytelling experience preferred. Valid driver's license with a good driving record and the ability to provide proof of insurance meeting company requirements. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Strong broadcast and AP-style writing skills with a commitment to accuracy and storytelling excellence. Experience with videography and non-linear video editing platforms. Knowledge of professional broadcast camera equipment and field production techniques. Proficiency editing video using Final Cut Pro or comparable editing systems. Comfortable posting and managing content across websites and digital platforms. Strong computer skills, including experience with newsroom computer systems. Excellent news judgment, time management, and organizational abilities. A self-starter mentality with the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Confidence working under pressure in a fast-paced, deadline-driven newsroom environment. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed in support of field reporting and production activities. OUR TEAM: At KPAX, you'll join a collaborative newsroom dedicated to delivering trusted local journalism. Our team brings together experienced journalists, creative storytellers, and passionate community advocates who support one another and share a commitment to serving viewers with integrity. We value diverse perspectives, innovative ideas, and a culture where curiosity, teamwork, and professional growth thrive. WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Nestled in the heart of western Montana, Missoula offers an unmatched combination of outdoor adventure, vibrant arts and culture, and a strong sense of community. Surrounded by mountains, rivers, and scenic trails, it's a destination for hiking, skiing, mountain biking, fishing, and year-round exploration. Beyond its natural beauty, Missoula is home to a thriving downtown, local breweries, live music, unique restaurants, and the University of Montana. job.title: Digital & Social Platform Editor
job.description:
Who we are

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Our editors and reporters distill the most important stories from all over in formats that uncover the forces shaping the stories, explain the interests behind polarizing narratives, and replenish the stock of shared facts. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on.

About the Role

Semafor is seeking a Digital & Social Platform Editor to help amplify our journalism across platforms and formats.

This is not a traditional “social posting” role. We’re looking for someone who understands how modern media travels — across video, live events, podcasts, breaking news, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, X, and emerging platforms. The right candidate understands that packaging and distribution is editorial — and an important part of propelling our journalism forward.

This role sits at the center of newsroom, audience, video, audio, and events. You’ll help shape the strategy for how Semafor’s journalism is framed, edited, clipped, promoted, and distributed in real time .

You should have strong editorial instincts, comfort with video and light editing workflows, sharp news and platform judgment, and a deep understanding of how to create platform-native content that drives reach without compromising editorial quality. Interest in business, politics, media, technology, and global affairs is important.

Responsibilities

Packaging & Distribution of Our Best Journalism

  • Work with newsroom leaders to identify the strongest moments, angles, and formats for distribution across scoops, breaking news, enterprise reporting, interviews, video, podcasts, and live journalism
  • Develop deep relationships with distribution platforms, with a special focus on LinkedIn, YouTube and X
  • Package and distribute Semafor journalism across social and digital platforms in formats optimized for each audience and channel
  • Write platform-native copy, headlines, captions, hooks, and framing that increase engagement and discoverability
  • Publish and optimize content across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging platforms

Video & Live Content

  • Support rapid-turnaround distribution from Semafor events, including clipping live mainstage conversations in real time, or editorial video
  • Knowledge of analytics, audience development, and platform performance trends
  • Interest in business, politics, media, technology, and global affairs
  • Work closely with video and audio producers to extend the reach and lifecycle of original content
  • Execute social video editing, formatting, subtitling, and platform optimization
  • Ability to clip, package, and publish short-form video from interviews, podcasts, newsroom shoots, and live events

Events & Promotion

  • Support promotional campaigns for Semafor events, franchises, and editorial launches
  • Coordinate social coverage plans and live posting during major convenings and newsroom moments
  • Help extend the reach of Semafor’s live journalism before, during, and after events
  • Develop and implement promotion plans for shows and big events across all platforms

Audience & Editorial Collaboration

  • Partner closely with the newsroom and audience teams to identify distribution opportunities and audience growth strategies
  • Apply editorial judgment to determine what content should travel, where it should live, and how it should be framed
  • Monitor performance trends, audience behavior, and platform shifts to inform publishing strategy
  • Maintain Semafor’s editorial standards, voice, and accuracy across all distributed content

Qualifications

  • 3-5 years of experience in social media, audience development, digital publishing, or platform distribution
  • Strong editorial instincts and understanding of news judgment
  • Experience publishing across major social and video platforms, with a particular focus on LinkedIn, YouTube, X, and Reddit
  • Understanding of platform-native storytelling and audience behavior
  • Ability to work quickly and calmly in a fast-paced newsroom and live event environment
  • Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
  • Experience covering or supporting live events
  • Familiarity with Premiere, CapCut, Descript, or similar editing tools
  • Experience working with a wide array of journalists, newsroom teams

Compensation: The salary range for this role is $100, 000 - $120,000 annually based on individual candidate experience and skills.

Additional job details

Semafor offers a Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) policy to our full-time, salaried employees who may take paid time off as-needed without a prescribed limit or defined balance.

Semafor, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and enthusiastically encourages people from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. Semafor, Inc. will consider all applicants without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical and/or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

job.title: Editorial Event Producer - Contract Opportunity
job.description:
Who we are

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Our editors and reporters distill the most important stories from all over in formats that uncover the forces shaping the stories, explain the interests behind polarizing narratives, and replenish the stock of shared facts. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on.

About this Role

As the Editorial Event Producer, you will work closely with Semafor’s Executive Editor and live journalism team to help produce our flagship global economic event. You will engage prospective guests, develop thoughtful programming recommendations, and manage multiple executive relationships with exceptional communication. The role requires the ability to speak fluently across industries and global economic issues, understand what makes an executive or policymaker compelling on stage, and connect their expertise to the broader editorial agenda.

You will take ownership of guest outreach and booking timelines, working proactively to move conversations forward and navigate complex organizations to reach the right people. You should be a resourceful, self-starting researcher who knows how to find information when it is not readily available, quickly get up to speed on unfamiliar companies, industries, and leaders. Throughout, you will bring strong editorial judgment, curiosity, creativity, and an entrepreneurial mindset to building a newsworthy, high-caliber program featuring some of the most influential leaders in business, government, technology, and finance.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own outreach and booking for a portfolio of senior executives, government leaders and other high-profile prospective guests for Semafor’s flagship economic event.
  • Identify contacts and pursue outreach with persistence, creativity, and sound judgment across executive offices, communications teams, and other channels.
  • Own outreach pipelines, leading follow-ups and updates as needed to secure commitments..
  • Serve as a compelling ambassador for Semafor, speaking fluently about the event’s editorial mission, audience, and value proposition and persuasively articulate why an executive should participate.
  • Leverage the strongest verbal communication skills when communicating with executive teams and exhibit professionalism, warmth, responsiveness and attention to detail throughout the booking process.
  • Lead pre-event editorial calls with executive teams to discuss programming, surfacing the most compelling areas for conversation and detailed notes for moderators.
  • Develop a strong understanding of each individual executive, their company, industry, and areas of expertise, articulating how each will contribute meaningfully to the broader program.
  • Apply strong editorial and strategic judgment to assess the relevance and significance of prospective guests and make thoughtful programming recommendations.

What makes you qualified

  • A Bachelor's degree is required.
  • 7+ years in broadcast journalism, executive communications, event content or programming development, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex editorial programs across dozens of speakers and sessions.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills and proven ability to engage confidently with senior-level executives.
  • Outstanding verbal and written communication, including the ability to craft compelling invitations and executive briefs.
  • Strongest organizational and time-management skills, adept at juggling multiple relationship streams.
  • Knowledgeable about major business and economic trends, along with skills to translate them into mainstage moments and other convenings for executives, with assistance from the editorial team.
  • An entrepreneurial drive grounded in an eagerness to learn and grow alongside the company as it continues to scale and evolve.
  • Passion for the media industry and great journalism.

Additional Job Details

This position is remote, though candidates based in Washington, DC, or New York, NY are preferred. Candidates must be willing to work flexible hours.

Salary Range:

Starting at $50.00 an hour. Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, certifications, etc.

The Role

Semafor is hiring an exceptional Lead Editor for its signature briefing, Flagship. Aimed at the core Semafor audience — senior executives, decision makers, and policymakers — Flagship distills the biggest, most important, and interesting news from across the world into tight, analytically rich, and deeply contextualized updates for sophisticated, time-poor readers. Its core strength is that it is complex, comprehensive, and completable.

The successful candidate will help run this product and infuse the Flagship sensibility across the Semafor newsroom, its products, site, and app. They will both write and edit with fluidity and should be armed in particular with strong associative intelligence — able to tie together complex ideas and seemingly disparate developments — alongside a deep understanding of the factors driving global geoeconomics, particularly when it comes to developments in technology, business, economics, finance, and trade. The Lead Editor will be skilled at making connections, implicit and explicit, across themes, geographies, and industries, while also bringing delight to readers’ daily lives. They will handle the news with sobriety and historical nuance.

The successful candidate will report to the Global Managing Editor, as part of a team of contributors worldwide, helping drive both daily editions of Flagship. They will be based in London.

Your responsibilities

  • Work with Semafor journalists to shape Flagship’s tone and coverage, and write most of it on a daily basis in the UK morning.
  • Support the production of the edition that publishes in the US evening with insights and ideas.
  • Collaborate across the Semafor newsroom, working with all our teams and verticals, contributing broadly to coverage beyond Flagship — in particular by writing, editing, or assigning stories.
  • Help lead the conception and execution of a Semafor app.
  • Write smart, sophisticated, analytically hefty updates for an elite audience.
  • Participate in event moderation, as well as media appearances on TV, radio, and podcasts.

What makes you qualified

  • 5 to 10 years of journalism experience, with a track record of major writing roles or leadership of high-level newsletters or briefings.
  • Experience and interest in global financial and business journalism.
  • A strategic, sophisticated approach to identifying themes and focuses of coverage across sectors and borders.
  • Bring speedy insight to big news stories, and flair and personality to writing.
  • A passion for world events and issues and a broad interest in a wide range of subjects.
  • Broad media consumption habits across conventional and unconventional sources.
  • Eagerness to be part of a dynamic work environment demanding initiative, flexibility, and a willingness to jump in wherever needed to help the team succeed.
  • Experience working with diverse teams with teammates from many different backgrounds.
  • Diligence and reliability to work without hands-on supervision.
  • The ability to think constantly about story distribution and audiences, across many forms of media and platforms.

What You’ll Do:

job.title: Senior Producer, Video & Live Journalism
job.description:
Who we are

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Our editors and reporters distill the most important stories from all over in formats that uncover the forces shaping the stories, explain the interests behind polarizing narratives, and replenish the stock of shared facts. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on.

About the Role

Semafor is seeking a Senior Producer, Video & Live Journalism to lead the editorial and production execution of our interview-led video programming, with an initial focus on conversations with CEOs and other consequential global decision-makers.

This person will play a central role in producing across a range of Semafor shows. Semafor brings policy makers and business leaders into substantive, newsworthy conversations about the decisions shaping their companies and the new world economy.

The Senior Producer will also help define how video extends the reach and impact of Semafor’s journalism. Working closely with the newsroom, audience, and live journalism teams, this person will shape the strategy around livestreams, what should be reimagined as on-demand programming, and how Semafor’s gatherings can generate distinctive video before, during, and after each event.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role. The ideal candidate can sharpen the editorial thesis of an interview, prepare a host for a high-stakes conversation, run a multi-camera production, give decisive notes in the edit, and use audience data to make the next episode better.

Responsibilities

  • Own interview shows from idea to publication. Lead the end-to-end production of CEO and executive interview programming, including editorial development, research, pre-interviews, host preparation, rundowns, scripts, production, post-production, and final publishing.

  • Work with hosts, reporters, and editors to identify the decisions, tensions, and moments of judgment that will produce candid, news-making interviews rather than conventional executive profiles.

  • Produce hosts and editorial talent. Help hosts refine their on-camera voice, interview approach, pacing, and chemistry. Provide clear feedback before, during, and after production.

  • Lead video production. Manage studio, field, remote, and event-based shoots, including crews, editors, lighting and audio teams, production vendors, schedules, budgets, travel, releases, and technical requirements.

  • Partner with the live-journalism and events teams to identify the sessions, speakers, and moments with the greatest video potential. Build capture and distribution plans that distinguish between live utility and durable, on-demand programming.

  • Extend the life of Semafor’s events. Create intentional packages around marquee events, including livestreams, full conversations, backstage interviews, field pieces, previews, recaps, and short-form excerpts.

  • Direct the edit and maintain a high creative bar. Shape long-form episodes, trailers, cold opens, promotional assets, and social cuts. Give precise notes on story structure, pacing, visuals, sound, graphics, and tone.

  • Build platform-native distribution plans. Work with Semafor’s audience team on titles, thumbnails, descriptions, chapters, clips, publishing cadence.

  • Use data to improve the journalism. Analyze audience retention, watch time, click-through rates, completion rates, returning viewers, and other platform-specific signals. Turn those insights into practical changes to format, packaging, episode structure, and distribution.

  • Build scalable production systems. Establish repeatable workflows, calendars, templates, review processes, and quality-control standards that allow Semafor to produce ambitious work consistently and efficiently.

  • Protect Semafor’s editorial standards. Ensure that scripts, interviews, edits, headlines, and promotional materials meet the highest standards for accuracy, fairness, transparency, and editorial independence.

Qualifications

  • At least 7 years of experience in a newsroom, broadcast organization, or digital news operation, with significant responsibility for video journalism or interview-led programming.
  • Exceptional editorial judgment and a strong grasp of business, economics, politics, technology, global affairs, and the forces affecting corporate leadership.
  • Experience working directly with prominent hosts, reporters, correspondents, executives, or public figures. You are comfortable operating around senior talent without becoming deferential or losing sight of the journalism.
  • A sophisticated understanding of YouTube and LinkedIn, including how audience expectations, packaging, tone, length, and measures of success differ across the two platforms.
  • Strong technical fluency across production and post-production. You do not need to perform every production function yourself, but you must understand cameras, lighting, audio, editing, livestreaming, and delivery well enough to make informed decisions.
  • An entrepreneurial approach and willingness to operate in a growing newsroom where the person defining the strategy is often also responsible for executing it.

Compensation: The salary range for this role is $130,000 - $160,000 annually based on individual candidate experience and skills.
